Heard Smt.Shaila Bellikatti, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri Ravindra R.Mane, learned counsel for the respondents.

2. The present appeal is directed against the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.220/2016 dated 11.12.2013 on the file of the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Belagavi.

entities.text: III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
A claim petition came to be filed under Section 166 of the M.V.Act, claiming compensation in respect of accidental injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident that occurred on 11.01.2013 at about 6.45 pm being pedestrian, on account of rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-22/EG-4117.
4.

Admitted facts are that the claim petition, on contest, came to be allowed in a sum of Rs.1,24,980/- with interest at NC: 2024:KHC-D:1093 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization, as under:
Loss of future income Rs.60,480/-
Pain and suffering Rs.10,000/-

sentences.text:
Medical expenses and other incidental expenses Rs.40,000/-
Loss of happiness and amenities Rs.10,000/-
Loss of income during treatment Rs.4,500/-
 TOTAL Rs.1,24,980/-
5.

On account of awarding of meager compensation,
claimant is in appeal.

6. Smt.Shaila Bellikatti, learned counsel for the appellant, reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of the appeal, contended that the notional income taken by the Tribunal while assessing loss of future prospects at Rs.4,500/-
is on the lower side.

7. As a stand and practice, for the accidental injuries of the year 2013, notional income is to be assessed in a sum of Rs.7,000/- and so also, on the other heads, award of NC: 2024:KHC-D:1093 compensation is on lower side and sought for enhancement of compensation.
8.
Per contra, Sri Ravindra R. Mane, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supports the impugned judgment and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
9. Perused the material on record meticulously.
Admittedly, there are fracture injuries sustained by the claimant.

Likewise, monthly income is assessed at Rs.4,500/- which needs to be considered in a sum of Rs.7,000/- while calculating the quantum of compensation on the ground of loss of future income in the absence of proper proof of income.

10. Hence, case has been made out for re-assessment of compensation which is as under:
Loss of future income Rs.94,080/-
(Rs.7,000x12x8x14/200)
Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-

Medical expenses and other incidental expenses Rs.35,275/-
Loss of happiness and amenities Rs.20,000/-
Loss of income during treatment Rs.21,000/-
Incidental expenses Rs.10,000/-

 ORDER  (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) As against the award of compensation in a sum of Rs.1,24,980/-, claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.2,05,355/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
(iii) Four weeks' time is granted for the Insurance Company to deposit the balance compensation.
